events.title: Death of Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor
events.description: Maximilian I of the House of Habsburg died at Wels, Austria. He had expanded Habsburg power through strategic marriages, including his own to Mary of Burgundy and the matches of his children and grandchildren.
events.significance: His death triggered the 1519 imperial election, won by his grandson Charles V, who inherited a vast Habsburg realm spanning Europe and the Americas.

events.title: First Public Museum in North America Opens
events.description: The Charleston Library Society voted to establish a museum in Charleston, South Carolina, widely regarded as the first public museum in the American colonies, dedicated to natural history.
events.significance: It marked the beginning of public museums in what would become the United States, promoting science and public education.

events.title: Death of Pierre de Fermat
events.description: French mathematician Pierre de Fermat died at Castres, France. A lawyer by profession, he made foundational contributions to number theory, probability, analytic geometry and optics, and posed the famous Last Theorem.
events.significance: Fermat's Last Theorem remained unsolved for over 350 years until Andrew Wiles proved it in 1994, driving major advances in mathematics.

events.title: Haiti Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, killing an estimated 100,000 to over 200,000 people and displacing more than a million.
events.significance: One of the deadliest natural disasters of the modern era, it prompted a massive international humanitarian response and exposed challenges in disaster relief and reconstruction.
